_meta.source: Authored for this app. Institutional facts follow data/pathways.json and data/subjects.json; NS staging follows public MINDEF enlistment norms; no private person or business is real.
_meta.notes: v2 content rules, linted where possible: every screen owns a concrete noun; public places are real, private ones invented; dialogue is allowed and Singlish is never mocked; one aphorism per string; school years are narrated from inside the age; the memoir voice is earned from 27 up. The NS chapters are asked for once, in fiction, and the answer is logged, never revisited. Every flag set here is read by a card or an outcome. Every door is granted somewhere and asked for somewhere.

wants.label: Be really good with my hands
Be there when people are struggling

d_mi.label: The three year A Level
d_mi.body: The same certificate, taken over three years instead of two.

d_pfp.label: The foundation year
d_pfp.body: A year that lands you inside a diploma cluster, already counted as one of theirs.

reflection.prompt: Name one thing you would do differently from here.
reflection.hint: Nobody marks this. It reappears when you compare two stories, in your own words.

stages.title: Sec 1
stages.situation: New school, new blazer, and by June you know which staircase floods. This year you take {subjects}, and everything is still moving.

choices.label: Try out for a CCA you have never done
choices.outcome: Wednesday trainings eat your evenings and hand you a second set of friends.
choices.missed: The trial happened without you. There is next year.

choices.label: Go to remedial for your weakest subject
choices.outcome: Thursday remedial with Mr Tan, week after week. October's paper comes back two grades kinder.
choices.missed: The Thursday remedial ran without you.

choices.label: Ask a teacher about taking a subject higher
choices.outcome: You ask. The answer is a maybe, then a yes, and the timetable changes.
choices.outcomeRaised: {subject} moves to {level} at year end. You asked, so it moved.
choices.missed: Nobody knew you wanted to move up, so nothing moved.

choices.label: Keep up what you did in primary school
choices.outcome: Wushu, or the keyboard, or the drawing. Old thing, new school, still yours.
choices.missed: The old thing goes quiet this year.

choices.label: Build a study routine you can actually keep
choices.outcome: Same desk, same hours, phone in the other room. It is dull in March and it is the reason October is calm.
choices.grew: learned to run your own week
choices.missed: The year ran on whatever each evening felt like.

choices.label: Make something after school and finish it
choices.outcome: A game in Scratch, a comic, a stool. Small, finished, and yours.

stages.title: Sec 2
stages.situation: Streaming is gone but the whisper survives at the void deck: which class are you in. This year the subject combination form is real, and {subjects} sit on your table.

choices.label: Train for the level you want in Sec 3
choices.outcome: You ask what the bar is, then train for it like a race.
choices.outcomeRaised: {subject} moves to {level}. The Sec 3 form changes shape because you asked.
choices.missed: The review meeting discussed other people.

choices.label: Read the whole subject booklet, not just the usual
choices.outcome: You read all of it, even Electronics, even Drama. Two subjects you had dismissed stop being jokes.
choices.missed: The booklet stayed unread, and the form got filled from hearsay.

choices.label: Take a real part in a performance or contest
choices.outcome: Concert, kids day, inter school heats. Your name gets read over a PA system.

choices.label: Coach a classmate who is falling behind
choices.outcome: You sit with the classmate everyone gave up on. Their D becomes a C, and they remember.
choices.missed: The classmate who was sinking found someone else, eventually.

choices.label: Find a place you can actually study
choices.outcome: Home is loud this year, so it becomes the library near the interchange, four to seven.

choices.label: Turn your hobby into something other people use
choices.outcome: Twelve people use the thing you made. Two send you bugs. You fix them.

stages.title: Sec 3
stages.situation: The combination is set: {subjects} now, all the way to the SEC. New class, some old faces missing, and suddenly teachers say the word portfolio out loud.

choices.label: Go deep on your strongest subject
choices.outcome: Past papers before anyone assigns them. The subject starts feeling like yours, not the school's.
choices.missed: Your best subject stayed merely good this year.

choices.label: Start collecting proof for Early Admissions
choices.outcome: Screenshots, certificates, the write up of the thing you built. Boring now, gold at Sec 4.
choices.missed: The folder stayed empty. Sec 4 will mean one panicked typing weekend.

choices.label: Take a leadership role in class or CCA
choices.outcome: Logistics IC for the CCA bazaar. Everything that can topple does, and you catch most of it.
choices.missed: Someone else carried the bazaar clipboard.

choices.label: Apply for the overseas immersion trip
choices.outcome: Ten days in a partner school in Chiang Mai or Fuzhou. You come back with a class group chat in two languages.
choices.missed: The immersion list closed with somebody else on it.

choices.label: Make something real that other people use
choices.outcome: The bake sale ordering sheet, the class tee design, the two minute film. Used by strangers, kept in your folder.

choices.label: Join a programme outside school
choices.outcome: Saturday coding, a science olympiad squad, youth theatre at the CC. Nobody from your class is there, which is the point.
choices.missed: The Saturday programme ran without you in it.

stages.title: Sec 4
stages.situation: SEC year. The class group chat becomes a study group chat, mostly. EAE opens before results, and everyone suddenly wants to know what Mother Tongue B3 converts to.

choices.label: Train for the papers like a sport
choices.outcome: Ten year series, timed, at the kitchen table. By September the fear is mostly gone.

choices.label: Keep sleep and exercise through the exam year
choices.outcome: You keep Sunday football and your sleep. Your mocks wobble, then hold.

choices.label: Ask a teacher what to fix first
choices.outcome: Ms D circles two questions in your script. Just these two habits, she says. She is right.
choices.missed: Nobody aimed the revision, so the weak paper stayed weak.

choices.label: Keep one thing going that is not the exam
choices.outcome: Fifteen minutes a night on the thing that is yours. The exam year does not eat it.

choices.label: Carry more of the house through the exam year
choices.outcome: You cook Tuesdays and quiz your sister for her PSLE. The house passes its exams together.

choices.label: Submit the Early Admissions application
choices.outcome: You write five hundred words about the thing you made and hit submit before you can chicken out.
choices.missed: The EAE window closed. It does not reopen. The main round remains.

stages.title: Results day
stages.situation: The envelope, in a hall that smells of floor polish. This is the moment that feels like a verdict, and is not one. Where do you point yourself?

choices.label: Junior College
choices.outcome: You pick the fast lane with the essays. Two years, one exam, and everything after it.

choices.label: Millennia Institute
Polytechnic
choices.outcome: You pick a field with a name and a lanyard. Three years of doing the actual thing.

choices.label: The Poly Foundation Year
ITE, Higher Nitec
choices.outcome: You pick the workshop over the lecture hall. The tools are real from day one.

choices.label: Higher Nitec, straight to year two
An arts school, on a portfolio
choices.outcome: You pick the interview where your folder does the talking. NAFA or LASALLE, work first.

choices.label: A fifth year, to widen it
choices.outcome: One more year at a harder level, aimed at a specific course. Slower, and it works.

stages.situation: One question before the next part. Around now, most Singaporean sons spend two years in uniform. Some serve before their course, some after. Is National Service part of your road?
Lectures run at double speed and the reading list is not a suggestion. Project Work locks five strangers into one grade. Everyone here was top of some class.

choices.label: Work out how to study at this level
choices.outcome: Notes you actually reread, a week that repeats, a tutor you stop avoiding. The jump stops feeling like a cliff.
choices.missed: Term three arrives before your study system does.

choices.label: Do your share of Project Work properly
choices.outcome: You chair the meetings nobody wants. The grade lands, and four people owe you.
choices.missed: The PW group limps without a chair.

choices.label: Run for a council or committee seat
choices.outcome: Council, or captain, or the fest committee. Your Tuesdays vanish and your circle triples.

choices.label: Keep one thing going outside lessons
choices.outcome: The film club edit, the fanzine, the app. JC does not get all of you.
choices.missed: The side thing hibernates under the reading list.

choices.label: Hold a job at weekends
choices.outcome: Cafe counter at Junction 8. Your own transport money, and a manager who rates you.

stages.situation: Prelims, then the real thing. The canteen empties after five as the study rooms fill. Someone laminates a countdown. It is a strange, close, purposeful year.

choices.label: Give the A Levels the whole year
choices.outcome: You train like it is a season. Whatever the slip says, you finish knowing you emptied the tank.

choices.label: Pace the year so you last it
choices.outcome: Badminton Thursdays survive the countdown. You walk into the hall level, not hollow.
choices.missed: The year became only the exam.

choices.label: Study with the same group every week
choices.outcome: Four of you, one whiteboard, economics until the library chases you out. The pack holds.

choices.label: Apply to more than one kind of course
choices.outcome: You read the poly EAE page and two overseas prospectuses anyway. Knowing the exits calms the corridor.
choices.missed: Plan B stayed unwritten.

stages.situation: A campus with escalators, modules with codes, and a GPA that starts counting from week one. Nobody checks your homework. That is the trap and the gift.

choices.label: Set up a routine in week one
choices.outcome: Deadlines in a calendar, readings before the lecture, one clear evening. Week ten arrives and nothing is on fire.
choices.missed: Semester one graded you while you were settling in.
choices.grew: set up a week that holds

choices.label: Get to know the people on your course
choices.outcome: Supper at the West Coast prata place after critique night. Half your future collaborators are at that table.
choices.missed: The supper table formed without you.

choices.label: Take small paid jobs in your field
choices.outcome: A real client, a real deadline, eighty real dollars. School suddenly has a point.

choices.label: Protect both your grades and your health
choices.outcome: Routine carries you: classes, training, home by eight. Boring, and it banks a 3.8 semester.

choices.label: Take a committee seat in a club
choices.outcome: You run orientation for two hundred freshies. Logistics, tears, one lost mascot head. People know you now.

stages.situation: Twenty weeks inside a real company, with a staff pass and a standup at nine fifteen. Your supervisor is thirty one and tired. What you do here follows you.

choices.label: Treat the attachment as a real job
choices.outcome: You take the ticket nobody wants and close it. On your last day the team lead says call me when you graduate.

choices.label: Collect every skill you can prove later
choices.outcome: You shadow the senior tech at every fault call. Half a diploma's learning happens in that van.
choices.missed: The attachment stayed the tasks on the sheet, and nothing past them.

choices.label: Ask the adults there how they got in
choices.outcome: How did you get here, you ask the quiet engineer. Nobody has asked her in years. She tells you everything.
choices.missed: Twenty lunches, headphones in.

choices.label: Keep your coursework going alongside it
choices.outcome: FYP proposal drafted on the evening MRT out of Tanjong Pagar. Tired, organised, on time.

stages.situation: Final year project, then the square hat. The group chat splits three ways: job offers, uni applications, and one guy going full time on his sneaker resale thing.

choices.label: Make your final year project the one you show
choices.outcome: The project gets shown at the school showcase. A stranger photographs your poster and emails you.

choices.label: Keep the people you want to keep
choices.outcome: Chalet at Pasir Ris, photos at the jetty. These are the numbers you will still have at forty.

choices.label: Chase a place on a degree course
choices.outcome: GPA, portfolio, personal statement. You apply to three courses and let the dice sit.
choices.missed: The uni application window slid past unopened.

choices.label: Take the job offer seriously
choices.outcome: The internship company calls back. A number with a comma in it, attached to your name.
choices.missed: The callback went to voicemail and then to someone else.

stages.situation: Coveralls, toe capped boots, and a lecturer who spent nineteen years fixing lifts before he taught it. The workshop smells of cut metal. You are sixteen minutes in and useful.

choices.label: Get a certificate employers actually ask for
choices.outcome: First aid, work at height, the basic WSQ modules. Cards in your wallet that mean sites will take you.
choices.missed: The cert runs filled up without your name.

choices.label: Learn from the lecturer who knows the trade
choices.outcome: Mr Rashid lets you strip the compressor twice. Ask him anything, he says, except for extensions.
choices.missed: Mr Rashid taught someone else his shortcuts.

choices.label: Take weekend work on a real site
choices.outcome: Your uncle's aircon crew in Tampines, Saturdays. Cash, sweat, and the fastest learning you have done.

choices.label: Build a work routine you can keep
choices.outcome: Tools back where they belong, hours logged, invoices on time. Boring, and it is why people rehire you.

choices.label: Fix things for neighbours and get known
choices.outcome: The kopitiam auntie's chiller, your neighbour's fan. Word gets around the block that you can fix.

stages.situation: End of Year 2. Leave now with a Nitec and start earning, or stay for Year 3 and the Higher Nitec. Uncle says money. Mr Rashid says finish.

choices.label: Stay and finish Year 3
choices.outcome: You stay for the Higher Nitec and the GPA that opens poly. The pay can wait a year.
choices.missed: The full time pay packet waits a year.

choices.label: Exit with the Nitec, work
choices.outcome: You take the Nitec and the job. The door back to Year 3 stays open, and you know where it is.
choices.missed: The workshop kept your seat warm anyway.

choices.label: Work part time and keep studying
choices.outcome: Stay enrolled, work the school holidays on payroll. Both uncles half satisfied, you fully stretched.

choices.label: Ask what your results would reach
choices.outcome: The ECG officer draws the ladder on scrap paper: 2.5 applies, raw 3.5 guarantees. You photograph it.
choices.missed: The exit decision got made on feel, with the GPA unread.

stages.situation: Final year. Industry attachment mornings, GPA arithmetic at night. The poly application window opens in January and your class talks about it at the bak chor mee stall.

choices.label: Line up the job first
choices.outcome: Two interviews before graduation, one offer in hand. Poly can happen later, from a desk that pays.
choices.missed: Results day arrived with nothing lined up behind it.

choices.label: Teach the first years what you know
choices.outcome: You run the Saturday remedial in the workshop. Explaining torque settings turns out to be how you master them.

choices.label: Push the grades as high as they go
choices.outcome: Raw 3.5 guarantees a poly place. You do the retest, keep the CCA points, and cross it.

choices.label: Make the attachment count for something
choices.outcome: The firm gives you the fault log nobody wants. You clear it, and the supervisor keeps your number.
choices.missed: The attachment stayed a timetable, not a foot in the door.

stages.situation: First crit. Your work goes on the wall and strangers discuss it like you are not there. Materials cost more than food this month. Happier and more scared than ever.

choices.label: Make more work than the brief asks for
choices.outcome: Thirty drawings where ten were asked. Quantity teaches what taste alone cannot.

choices.label: Learn to take criticism of your work
choices.outcome: You stop defending and start noting. The work improves the week you stop bleeding on it.
choices.missed: Every crit still feels like a verdict on you.

choices.label: Take small paid jobs on the side
choices.outcome: A menu for the zi char at Blk 214, a logo for a cousin's bakery. Paid twice, printed once.
choices.missed: The paying gigs went to someone hungrier.

choices.label: Find the material you want to work in
choices.outcome: Riso, clay, After Effects, thread. One of them answers you back. You marry it.

choices.label: Wait tables at weekends
choices.outcome: Dim sum service pays for the paint. Your feet hate you and your ledger balances.

stages.situation: The year the folder becomes a body of work. An open call at the library gallery, a zine fair at Bras Basah, a brand hunting student artists.

choices.label: Answer an open call for work
choices.outcome: Two pieces in a real gallery for three weeks. Your grandmother comes twice and tells the invigilator.
choices.missed: The gallery wall hung other people's work.

choices.label: Sell your work at a fair or market
choices.outcome: You sell forty three copies at five dollars and trade the rest. The table beside yours becomes a collaborator.
choices.missed: The fair happened one table short.

choices.label: Practise without chasing attention
choices.outcome: A thousand hours of unglamorous practice. The jump in your work is visible from across the room.

choices.label: Assist somebody already doing the work
choices.outcome: You stretch canvas and hold lights for someone mid career. You learn what the job actually is.
choices.missed: The studio assistant post went in a day.

stages.situation: Grad show year. Everything goes on one wall with your name under it. Aunties ask what job this becomes; the honest answer is several, stitched together, at first.

choices.label: Make the graduation show count
choices.outcome: You rebuild the piece three times. On opening night a design studio leaves a card on your plinth.

choices.label: Line up two or three sources of income
choices.outcome: Two teaching gigs, one retainer, weekend markets. A spreadsheet that adds up to rent.
choices.missed: Month one after graduation starts with zero invoices.

choices.label: Photograph and write up everything you made
choices.outcome: Photographed, captioned, on a site with your name as the URL. Future clients find you because of tonight.

choices.label: Apply for a degree top up
choices.outcome: UAS degree, or overseas with a scholarship folder. You ask the lecturers to grade your odds honestly.
choices.missed: The degree deadline passed while the show consumed you.

stages.situation: Tekong. The haircut, the duffel bag, a bunk of strangers: JC boy, poly boy, ITE boy, one guy who paints. Whatever you were outside, the field levels it by Wednesday.

choices.label: Master the vocation given
choices.outcome: Signals, or medic, or transport. Not what you asked for, and you get quietly excellent at it.
choices.missed: The vocation stayed a chore you did adequately.

choices.label: Be the one who holds the bunk together
choices.outcome: You talk the homesick recruit off the ledge at two am. The bunk group chat will outlive the army.
choices.missed: The bunk stayed twelve strangers sharing a ceiling.

choices.label: Use your weekends to keep learning
choices.outcome: Weekends: an online cert, driving lessons, the language app. The two years will not be a blank.

choices.label: Get a licence that counts outside
choices.outcome: Class three, paid for by the army, passed on the second try. It is useful for the next thirty years.
choices.missed: The licence stayed a thing to do later.

choices.label: Put yourself forward for command school
choices.outcome: You shout commands you once ignored. Leading tired people politely turns out to be a career skill.

stages.situation: The countdown app hits double digits. Half the bunk applies to uni on cookhouse wifi; the poly grads compare job ads on guard duty. ORD loh, someone yells, hourly.

choices.label: Apply for what comes next straight away
choices.outcome: Applications submitted from the mess table between duties. Your start date exists before your ORD date.
choices.missed: ORD arrived with no plan behind it, and the gap stretched.

choices.label: Write down every skill you were trained in
choices.outcome: Licences, logistics, the medic cert. You leave with paper civvie employers actually read.

choices.label: Stay in touch with the people you served with
choices.outcome: Supper at Al Azhar after every book out. Fifteen numbers from four different roads, all yours now.
choices.missed: The bunk chat went quiet before the cake did.

choices.label: Save the allowance properly
choices.outcome: Allowance is small so you make it deliberate. You ORD with a four figure buffer and options.

choices.label: Put the payout into a course
choices.outcome: The lump sum goes into a certificate instead of a phone. Nobody at the time thinks this is the fun choice.
choices.missed: The payout went the way payouts go.

stages.situation: Matriculation, a hall room that fits a bed and an ego, modules you finally chose yourself. Somewhere between orientation and final year project, you pick who you are becoming.

choices.label: Go deep in your major
choices.outcome: Honours track, a prof who knows your name, a thesis you almost enjoy. Depth compounds.
choices.missed: The major stayed a timetable instead of becoming a craft.

choices.label: Take a semester on exchange abroad
choices.outcome: Six months in another country on a student budget. You come back with range and a group chat in two time zones.

choices.label: Build something of your own alongside
choices.outcome: The app, the podcast, the thesis turned tool. Strangers use it, which no grade can buy.
choices.missed: The side project stayed a note on your phone.

choices.label: Work the career fairs properly
choices.outcome: Coffee chats, resume clinics, two internships. Graduation is an on ramp, not a cliff.
choices.missed: The careers office knew everyone's name except yours.

stages.situation: The first full month of pay lands with a payslip you read twice. CPF is real now, and so is the question of whether this job teaches you anything.

choices.label: Learn the job until it is easy
choices.outcome: You become the one who actually reads the manual. Within a year the escalations route to you.
choices.missed: Competence arrived on schedule instead of early.

choices.label: Build money habits while it is easy
choices.outcome: A budget you keep, three months put aside, CPF understood. It buys you the freedom to say no later.
choices.missed: The pay came and went without a plan.

choices.label: Keep one thing that pays on the side
choices.outcome: Weekend shoots, tuition classes, small builds. A second income with your own name on it.

choices.label: Keep showing up for the people around you
choices.outcome: Dinner at home Sundays, and you say out loud what you are working towards. They stop guessing.
choices.missed: Home kept guessing what you were up to.

choices.label: Start a part time qualification
choices.outcome: Work Study route: employed, paid, studying. Tuesday nights hurt and the certificate is real.

stages.situation: Another decade on this road would be fine. On your phone: a course brochure, a job ad, a business name you doodled. Pick the next stretch.

choices.label: Go deep, become the expert
choices.outcome: You choose mastery where you stand. The next thousand hours make you the person they phone first.

choices.label: Switch fields on purpose
choices.outcome: You trade seniority for range and start again on purpose. The beginner months are humbling and short.

choices.label: Upgrade while working
choices.outcome: SkillsFuture route: part time degree, employer nodding, weekends gone. The qualification lands at thirty.

choices.label: Start the thing, small
choices.outcome: Registered on ACRA in a lunch break. One client, then two. You keep the day job while it breathes.

choices.label: Choose the people years
choices.outcome: Family, or caring, or the community thing that needs hands. Work holds steady while life takes the lead.

stages.situation: The thirties go brick by brick. The career either compounds now or plateaus quietly, and the difference is mostly what you learn on purpose while nobody is asking you to.

choices.label: Take the job that means leading people
choices.outcome: Managing is a different job from doing, and nobody trains you. You learn on live humans, gently.

choices.label: Stay the person who does the work
choices.outcome: You decline the manager track twice. Your work gets quoted, forked, photographed. No regrets, most days.
choices.missed: The lead role went to someone who wanted it less.

choices.label: Grow the side thing into something bigger
choices.outcome: The folder of work becomes the pitch. You quote a real number, they pay it, and the weekend thing hires you.

choices.label: Teach what you know to somebody newer
choices.outcome: Adjunct evenings at your old school, or workshops at the CC. Explaining the craft renews it.
choices.missed: The teaching slot went unstaffed another year.

choices.label: Put the people at home first this year
choices.outcome: Parents aging, maybe kids arriving, definitely laundry. You resize ambition to fit love, on purpose.

stages.situation: Thirty eight. Not a crisis, just a clear evening and an honest mirror. The want you named as a teenager is still yours, or has quietly become something else.
A subject combination form is on your table again. Not yours: a thirteen year old you love is watching your face for a verdict. You remember this exact silence.

choices.label: Tell them what nobody told you
choices.outcome: Nothing on this form can close your life, you say. You watch their shoulders come down an inch.
choices.missed: The kid decoded your silence as a verdict anyway.

choices.label: Walk an open house with them
choices.outcome: Poly, ITE and JC open houses in one season, both of you asking questions. Their shortlist doubles.
choices.missed: They shortlisted from hearsay instead of visits.

choices.label: Vouch for somebody starting out
choices.outcome: A reference letter, an intro, a first gig. The people who once vouched for you taught you the move.

choices.label: Use your SkillsFuture credit
choices.outcome: The four thousand dollar top up at forty, spent on a course you chose like an adult. Homework at your age, gladly.

choices.label: Rebuild the year around what matters now
choices.outcome: Fewer hours, closer commute, one deliberate downshift. The trade is explicit and you sign it.

stages.situation: Forty eight. One classmate just retrained as a nurse; the wedding relative who judged ITE now asks your advice. The road behind you looks nothing like the form at fourteen.

choices.label: Mentor somebody on purpose
choices.outcome: You take two juniors seriously, the way Mr Rashid took you. It is the best interest rate you have found.
choices.missed: The juniors figured it out slower, alone.

choices.label: Learn the new tool anyway
choices.outcome: The software that was supposed to replace you becomes the thing you wield. Younger colleagues notice.

choices.label: Turn the trade into your own shop
choices.outcome: Your name above a door, your hours on it. Thirty years of hands finally on your own invoice.

choices.label: Bank the last conversions
choices.outcome: The subsidised diploma at any age is real money on the table. You take the class with the nineteen year olds.

choices.label: Rest, visibly
choices.outcome: You model something rare at your age: enough. The younger ones need to see it done once.

stages.situation: Three years instead of two, and everybody outside assumes that means something went wrong. Inside, the pace is the point: the same syllabus with room to breathe in it.

choices.label: Use the extra year properly
choices.outcome: The subject that beat you in Sec 4 becomes the one you explain to other people.
choices.missed: The extra year passed at the same speed as the others.

choices.label: Take the commerce subjects seriously
choices.outcome: Accounts and management stop being filler. A cluster of poly and university courses quietly opens.
choices.missed: The commerce papers stayed a timetable, not an interest.

choices.label: Answer the question about your school
choices.outcome: You get a short honest sentence ready. Saying it out loud a few times makes it true.
choices.missed: The question about the school kept getting answered by other people.

choices.label: Find the two who also want it
choices.outcome: Two of you start meeting in the library on Fridays. It becomes the reason the year works.
choices.missed: Three years of Fridays in a library full of people, alone.

choices.label: Go hard at one A Level subject
choices.outcome: You pick one and drive it. Depth in one paper reads better than flatness across four.
choices.missed: Every subject got the same middling hour.

stages.situation: A year inside the polytechnic before the diploma formally starts. You have a student card, a campus, and a cluster full of people who arrived the same way you did.

choices.label: Treat it as year zero of the diploma
choices.outcome: You learn the campus, the lecturers and the library before any of it counts. The head start is real.
choices.missed: The foundation year passed as a waiting room instead of a year one.

choices.label: Pick the course inside the cluster carefully
choices.outcome: You sit in on two courses you were not sure about. One of them turns out to be yours.
choices.missed: The course inside the cluster got chosen for you by default.

choices.label: Get the maths solid now
choices.outcome: The bridging module is not glamorous. It is the thing that stops year one from being a scramble.
choices.missed: The maths gap followed you into the diploma.

choices.label: Know the people who arrived like you
choices.outcome: The foundation cohort becomes a group of people who understand the exact route you took.
choices.missed: The cohort stayed a room of strangers who took the same route.

choices.label: Enter a cluster competition
choices.outcome: You build something with three strangers and lose, publicly, and learn more than the winners did.
choices.missed: The competition happened without you in it.

stages.situation: Half the people you sat beside in Sec 4 are somewhere with a shaved head, and you are already here. Two years is a long time to be early with.

choices.label: Get ahead in the course
choices.outcome: You take the heavier semester while it is quiet. Later, when it is loud, you have room.
choices.missed: The early quiet got spent the same as any other term.

choices.label: Take the internship nobody wanted
choices.outcome: An unglamorous attachment in a real place. You leave knowing how a workplace actually runs.
choices.missed: The attachment went to somebody who asked for it.

choices.label: Start something of your own
choices.outcome: Small, unfinished, entirely yours. It teaches you what you like more accurately than any quiz.
choices.missed: The idea stayed a note in your phone.

choices.label: Keep the group chat alive
choices.outcome: You are the one who remembers birthdays and books out weekends. Two years later the friendships are still there.
choices.missed: Two years of distance did what distance does.

choices.label: Take on something that runs the place
choices.outcome: A committee, a shop floor, a team. Being responsible for other people's Tuesdays changes you.
choices.missed: Nobody's Tuesday depended on you.

stages.situation: The others come back changed and full of stories about a field. You have two years of your own behind you, and nobody hands you a certificate for them.

choices.label: Say what you did with them
choices.outcome: You get clear about what those two years were for. It turns out to be a longer answer than you expected.
choices.missed: The two years stayed hard to describe, even to yourself.

choices.label: Convert the work into a qualification
choices.outcome: The hours you already put in count towards something official. Paperwork, then a certificate.
choices.missed: The experience stayed real but unrecorded.

choices.label: Take the harder module now
choices.outcome: You use the standing you built to get into something that would have been closed to you at seventeen.
choices.missed: The safe module got taken, and finished, and taught nothing.

choices.label: Be the one who welcomes them back
choices.outcome: You help three people restart. Reorienting somebody else clarifies where you got to yourself.
choices.missed: They came back and worked it out alone.

choices.label: Go somewhere for a while
choices.outcome: A stint away, paid for carefully. You come home with a different sense of what is normal.
choices.missed: The trip stayed a tab you never closed.

endingFrames.head: You wanted to make things people use.
endingFrames.body: Count what exists because you do: the shipped work, the fixed machines, the printed pages. Strangers touch things you made without knowing your name, which is what making always promised.

endingFrames.head: You wanted to make things people use.
endingFrames.body: The surprise is that your making became a team sport. The things exist because you learned to gather people around a bench and keep them there.

endingFrames.head: You wanted to be good with your hands.
endingFrames.body: You are. The proof is in call backs and referrals, in the neighbour who trusts nobody else with the compressor. Skill this physical cannot be faked and was never obsolete.

endingFrames.head: You wanted to be there when people struggle.
endingFrames.body: Count who calls you first when it goes wrong. That list is your actual CV, and it took thirty years of showing up to write.

endingFrames.head: You wanted to be there when people struggle.
endingFrames.body: You learned the hard version: care with competence attached. The kindness got trained, certified and rostered, and it holds up at three in the morning.

endingFrames.head: You wanted to run your own thing.
endingFrames.body: Whether the name above the door is yours yet or not, you have run things for years: budgets, crews, risks taken with your own signature. Ownership turned out to be a habit before it was a registration.

endingFrames.head: You wanted to work out how things work.
endingFrames.body: You never stopped. The subjects changed names; the itch survived every timetable. People bring you broken systems the way others bring gossip, and you are glad.

endingFrames.head: You wanted every detail exactly right.
endingFrames.body: The world paid you for precisely this: the audits passed, the doses checked, the builds that do not wobble. Rigour turned out to be a form of care.

endingFrames.head: At the start you said you were not sure.
endingFrames.body: That was the honest answer, and it worked. You tried things, kept what fit and folded the rest, which is not indecision. It is how the sure people actually got sure.

endingFrames.head: Your road, with two years in green.
endingFrames.body: The uniform years slowed the paper and fed the person: strangers became brothers, and you learned to be depended on. Every date after shifted two years, and nothing worth having fell off the road.

endingFrames.head: Your road, walked your way.
endingFrames.body: Same start as thousands, same ending as no one. The doors you hold were opened by asking, making and showing up, none of which was printed on the form at fourteen.
